content:
anya: Quick sync — Q3 sprint gating: ACME asked to onboard their fine-tuned 13B ASAP, but we also have the general catalog backlog and a long bench queue. Need to pick lane strategy by EOD tomorrow.

mike: capacity-wise we can carve 1 GPU pool for a fastlane canary for ~48h, but it will bump queued onboarding jobs.

sam: What are the bench acceptance criteria for the fastlane? We should avoid lowering standard bar.

anya: Proposal: two lanes — 1) fastlane (customer-exception) with elevated SLA, soft-pin TTL 30d, mandatory mini-canary (500 samples) + perf baseline; 2) standard onboarding with full bench suite and staggered rollout.

liz: For fastlane, I want automatic fallback routing to a compatibility shim if issues detected. Canary should include traffic shaping: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 6h if metrics stable.

dave: From sales — ACME wants low-latency checks and pin until they finish re-eval. They're okay with a 30d soft-pin if we provide canary metrics and rollback window.

jen: CS: need a comms template for customers if we soft-pin. Also log what we promised in the contract (TTL + gracepath).

sam: Bench spec for fastlane mini-canary (proposed):
```
bench run --model acme-13b-ft --suite mini_canary --samples 500 \
  --metrics latency_p50,latency_p95,token_cost,embed_cosine,toxicity_score
```
Pass if: latency_p95 < 450ms, embed_cosine > 0.87 vs baseline, no regression > 2% on quality probes, toxicity_score within normal.

mike: Need to reserve a dedicated pool with pre-warmed KV cache for the canary samples to avoid cold-start bias. That adds ~20% infra cost for the window.

anya: Tradeoffs noted. If we do fastlane we charge an onboarding premium to cover infra and expedited ops.

bench-bot: new benchmark artifacts uploaded: /bench/archive/1792501234/acme-mini-canary-2026-03-23.json (500 samples)

sam: I reviewed the mini-canary artifacts — quick hits: latency_p95 = 420ms, embed_cosine = 0.892, small hallucination uptick on one probe (1.9% -> 2.6%). Need to confirm if that probe is blocker.

liz: Ops: if hallucination regressions >2% we trigger immediate soft-fallback to baseline model and open a ticket to model team. That's our safety gate.

dave: ACME will accept a fallback policy as long as we notify them and provide a timeline for fix.

anya: Decision call: do we approve fastlane for ACME now? Options: A) Approve with soft-pin 30d + premium + canary + auto-fallback; B) Push them to standard lane (full bench, longer runway); C) Hybrid: start with 48h limited fastlane (internal traffic only) then re-evaluate.

sam: I vote C — limited fastlane internal-only gives us data without customer risk.

mike: +1 for C. Limits infra exposure and keeps queue moving.

jen: +1 for C, and CS will prep comms for both outcomes.

liz: I'll own the rollout automation (canary gates + fallback). Will create runbook and a small playbook for on-call.

anya: OK consensus = C. Action items:
- liz: create canary automation + runbook (due 2026-03-25)
- sam: finalize mini-canary probe list + threshold doc (due 2026-03-24)
- mike: reserve pool and estimate infra premium cost for billing (due 2026-03-24)
- jen/dave: finalize ACME contract addendum for soft-pin + premium (due 2026-03-25)

anya: I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow 10:30 to unblock. If the mini-canary passes internal-only, we'll open the limited fastlane slot.

mike: I'll post pool sizing and cost numbers in #eng-infra once done.

sam: I'll push the bench job and tag you all when artifacts land.

bench-bot: scheduled bench job started: job_id=bb-179250-1 (500 samples)

anya: Thanks team — want minimal customer risk and a repeatable playbook for future requests. We'll capture learnings and turn this into a short 'fastlane' SOP after. :white_check_mark:
